newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton falls on poor demand, higher supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton falls on poor demand, higher supply.

text.p: Cotton prices suffered a setback on Tuesday on sluggish demand from yarn and textile mills and improved supplies, dealers said.
They said the progress of monsoon rains in cotton growing regions prompted selling by traders. Concern over a slight delay in the arrival of monsoon had now passed, they said.
Cotton supply had been adequate despite poor arrivals as the bulk of the 1996/97 (October/September) crop had already reached the market, traders said.

In spot, Bengal-deshi lost 10/15 rupees to 1,030/1,080 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned 40/50 rupees to 1,800/1,850 rupees per maund and F-414 10/15 rupees to 2,075/2,100 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) fell 100 rupees to 14,400/14,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
